scenes.tts: Picture a drop of pond water under a microscope. A Paramecium swims across it. It is one cell, shaped a bit like a slipper. That one cell moves, eats, and gets rid of extra water and wastes. It can also divide in two. Your body does the same kinds of jobs. So why does your body have trillions of cells?
scenes.visual: pond drop, Paramecium swims, job chips appear, cell divides, question
scenes.narration: Picture a drop of pond water under a microscope. A Paramecium swims across it. It is one cell, shaped a bit like a slipper. That one cell moves, eats, and gets rid of extra water and wastes. It can also divide in two. Your body does the same kinds of jobs. So why does your body have trillions of cells?

scenes.tts: A living thing made of just one cell is called unicellular. A Paramecium is unicellular. Short, hair-like parts called cilia beat to push it along. Food goes into small sacs called food vacuoles. A sac called a contractile vacuole squeezes out extra water. One cell has parts for every life job.
scenes.narration: A living thing made of just one cell is called unicellular. A Paramecium is unicellular. Short, hair-like parts called cilia beat to push it along. Food goes into small sacs called food vacuoles. A sac called a contractile vacuole squeezes out extra water. One cell has parts for every life job.

scenes.tts: A living thing made of many cells is called multicellular. You are multicellular, and so is an oak tree. In a many-celled body, cells share the work. This sharing is called division of labor. A specialized cell has a shape and parts that suit one kind of job.
scenes.visual: grid of cells, groups take jobs
scenes.narration: A living thing made of many cells is called multicellular. You are multicellular, and so is an oak tree. In a many-celled body, cells share the work. This sharing is called division of labor. A specialized cell has a shape and parts that suit one kind of job.

scenes.tts: Look at some shapes. A muscle cell is long and thin. It shortens to pull on bones. A nerve cell has long branches. It carries signals over long distances. A red blood cell is a small, flexible disc. It carries oxygen and bends through very narrow vessels.
scenes.narration: Look at some shapes. A muscle cell is long and thin. It shortens to pull on bones. A nerve cell has long branches. It carries signals over long distances. A red blood cell is a small, flexible disc. It carries oxygen and bends through very narrow vessels.

scenes.tts: In many multicellular organisms, such as you, cells are grouped into levels. Similar cells doing one job form a tissue, such as muscle tissue. Different tissues working together form an organ, such as the heart. Organs working together form an organ system, such as the heart and blood vessels. All the systems together make the organism.
scenes.narration: In many multicellular organisms, such as you, cells are grouped into levels. Similar cells doing one job form a tissue, such as muscle tissue. Different tissues working together form an organ, such as the heart. Organs working together form an organ system, such as the heart and blood vessels. All the systems together make the organism.

scenes.tts: The levels depend on each other. If heart tissue is damaged, the whole body can suffer. So how can one cell do everything a whole body does? A Paramecium does it with the parts of one cell. A body shares the jobs among trillions of cells, grouped into tissues, organs and organ systems.
